:::{#hero-heading}

<p style="text-align: justify;">I am a Postdoctoral Fellow at UC Santa Barbara, working with [Rafael J.P. Schmitt](https://es.ucsb.edu/people/rafael-jp-schmitt) on optimizing sustainable hydropower and riverine connectivity. In October 2026, I will be joining [Albert Ruhí](https://ruhilab.org/) at UC Berkeley as a [Croucher Fellow](https://croucher.org.hk/en/fellows-and-scholars/jeffery-chan?page=1) to investigate how extreme events are reshuffling diadromous fishes. Currently, I'm also awaiting my PhD defense at The University of Hong Kong, where I had the privilege of working with [David Dudgeon](https://www.biosch.hku.hk/ecology/dd.htm) and [Jia Huan Liew](https://discover.utas.edu.au/JiaHuan.Liew) on the impacts of fragmentation by dams on diadromous species at global and regional scales. Previously, I earned an MRes in Tropical Forest Ecology from Imperial College London examining  multiple-stressor interactions on ecosystem functioning using pond mesocosms (I was landlocked during covid). Prior to my academic journey I founded [Freshwater Collective](https://www.freshwatercollective.org), a conservation organization with the aim of bridging the gap between research and education of freshwater ecology.</p> 

My [Full CV](files/Jeffery_Chan_CV_Mar2026.pdf) (updated Mar 2026)
